title: What number of flowers stands for all five days?
description: Five columns of hibiscus flowers have different heights. The board adds them, divides by the number of days, and then levels the columns to the same height. Keeko doubts that the mean must be one of the counts.
teaching_notes: One idea: the average is the equal number each day would have after levelling, so it need not be any day's count. Watch for students who pick the average from the list of counts.

source: Vaishnavi counted 2, 7, 9, 4 and 3 hibiscus flowers blooming
video_script.why: The child can divide a total by a count but has not seen what the answer means or why it can be a number that no day shows.
video_script.substitution: The average is the equal level that the five daily counts reach when they are evened out.
video_script.anchor: Five columns of hibiscus flowers, one for each day, with different heights
video_script.wrong_answer: the mean has to be one of the counts
video_script.wrong_move: picks the mean from the list of counts instead of evening the days out
video_script.payoff_line: On average, five flowers bloom each day

final_answer.spoken: five flowers per day on average

names.Ziva: counts the hibiscus flowers that bloom each day

maths_rules: levelling: 9 gives 4 to 2, 7 gives 2 to 3, and 6 gives 1 to 4, so every day shows 5
5 is not one of the counts 2, 7, 9, 4, 3
video_script.design: Five columns of different heights. The board adds, divides, and then moves flowers from the tall columns to the short ones until all five are level.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; five columns of hibiscus flowers of different heights, one column for each day

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the garden and the five columns of flowers appear
marks.m3: the five columns show their counts, one after another
marks.m4: a question mark rises over the columns

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is an example from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ziva counts the hibiscus flowers blooming in a garden each day.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>On five days the counts are two, seven, nine, four and three.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What one number of flowers can stand for all five days?

beats.on_screen: the five columns stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a level line is drawn across the five columns; the number of flowers on that line is labelled average

marks.g1: a level line is drawn across the five columns
marks.g2: the label average appears on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Imagine the same number of flowers blooming on every day.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>That number is called the average of the daily counts.

beats.on_screen: Given: Ziva counted 2, 7, 9, 4, 3 hibiscus flowers on 5 days

marks.given: the five daily counts are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Ziva counted two, seven, nine, four and three flowers on five days.

beats.on_screen: To find: the average number of flowers per day, and what it means

marks.find: the words average and per day are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the average number of flowers per day, and say what it means.

marks.s1: the five columns slide into one heap

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add the flowers of all the days to get the total.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Two plus seven plus nine plus four plus three makes twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, average = total ÷ number of days: 25 ÷ 5 = 5

marks.d1: the rule average = total ÷ number of days is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, the average is the total divided by the number of days.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Twenty five divided by five gives five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, meaning: if every day had the same count, each day would show 5

marks.c1: the heap is dealt out equally over the five days
marks.c2: every column rises or falls to the level line

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, see what the five means.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>If every day had the same number of flowers, each day would have five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check by levelling: 9 gives 4 to 2; 7 gives 2 to 3; 6 gives 1 to 4; every column shows 5

marks.e1: four flowers move from the column of 9 to the column of 2
marks.e2: two flowers move from the column of 7 to the column of 3
marks.e3: one flower moves from the column of 6 to the column of 4, and all five columns are level

narration: <bookmark mark='e1'/>Step four, check by levelling the columns.
The day with nine gives four flowers to the day with two.
<bookmark mark='e2'/>The day with seven gives two flowers to the day with three.
<bookmark mark='e3'/>The day that now has six gives one flower to the day with four.
All the days show five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 5 flowers per day on average
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>On average, five flowers bloom each day.
That is the level the five daily counts reach when they are evened out.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's thought bubble points at the column of 7; the five columns then level to 5, a number that no column began with, and the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble points at the column of 7
marks.fix: the five columns level out to the same height

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the mean has to be one of the counts, so it picks seven.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the mean is not picked from the list, it comes from evening the days out.
<bookmark mark='idea'/>The number we reach may not be any day's count at all.
